approved: Road Vehicle Standards (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2018
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill supports the switch from the Motor Vehicle Standards Act 1989 to a new Road Vehicle Standards Bill 2018.
It provides a twelve-month transition period during which the old law continues to apply so industry can adjust.
Certain approval holders under the old law can use their existing evidence to get new approvals under the new law.
Repeals the Motor Vehicle Standards Act when the Road Vehicle Standards Bill starts.
Makes transitional rules for regulating vehicles during the changeover.
Amends other Commonwealth laws to replace references to the old Act with the new one.
Industry stakeholders and the general public who have rights or obligations under the old law.

The Road Vehicle Standards Bill 2018 and its transitional bill were moved for second reading, aiming to modernize vehicle import regulation with a 12‑month transition period and repeal the Motor Vehicle Standards Act 1989.

Labor supported the Road Vehicle Standards package, which replaces the Motor Vehicle Standards Act, creates an online register of approved vehicles, and is projected to reduce industry compliance costs by $68 million, while noting stakeholder concerns about impacts on small workshops and campervan converters.

The Road Vehicle Standards Bill 2018 and four companion bills were presented as a modern framework for regulating road vehicles, projected to save industry an estimated $20 million, establish the Register of Approved Vehicles (saving around $14 million a year), and introduce compulsory recall powers. The government announced amendments to allow used-vehicle imports for campervan/motorhome conversions, adjust power-to-weight thresholds for specialist vehicles, permit left-hand-drive heavy vehicles, and presented addenda to the explanatory memoranda following the Scrutiny of Bills committee's recommendations.
